newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Jan 7 - In early December we had warned a further slowdown in palm production growth. Growth in November had slowed to 2.6 percent from 8.9 percent in January-October. Latest data for December turned out poorer than we had expected when CPO output for the month shrank 3.4 percent to an estimated 630,000 tonnes. On a month-on-month basis, the seasonal decline came out at 17.4 pct as against our previous tentative estimate of 15 pct. This was caused partly by poorer than expected output in Sabah because of monsoon rains and floods which struck the state in the last week of December.

Production for the country for the 12 months to December totalled 8.3 million tonnes. This represents a growth of 7.3 percent or 568,000 tonnes over 1995. There was a marked improvement in the weather so far this month - in P.Malaysia as well as in Sabah and Sarawak. Indications are that the moonsson is over and the seasonal downtrend in production this month should be moderate. While CPO output fell more than 130,000 tonnes in December compared to Nov, offtake was down by some 10,000 tonnes only. The better than expected offtake was contributed by a jump in CPO exports to around 20,000 tonnes from a mere 1,000 tonnes in Nov reported by PORLA.

The sharp decline in CPO production resulting in a drawdown in stocks of about 120,000 tonnes to an estimated 485,000 at end-December. Concomitmment with the reduction in CPO supplies, end-December stocks of PPO fell some 30,000 tonnes to around 320,000 tonnes. Exports of PPO in December are estimated at 660,000 tonnes, up from the preliminary figure of 631,000 tonnes for November reported by PORLA. The higher exports reflected chiefly increased offtake by Islamic countries in West Asia in anticipation of growth in consumption during the Ramadan period in January/February. Total palm oil stocks at end December thus amounted to an estimated 805,000 tonnes.

This amount represents a big reduction of some 150,000 tonnes from a month earlier. Compared to December 1995, stocks were also lower by nearly 55,000 tonnes. In anticipation of improving fundamentals, CPO futures advanced 45 to 48 ringgit in the second half of December. The market pulled back five to eight ringgit at the start of the New Year but renewed shortcovering activities in the last two days saw prices recovered 13 to 23 ringgit. Yesterday, March futures settled at 1,260 ringgit while spot position settled at 1,273 ringgit. CPO physicals for January delivery in Pasir Gudang were traded at around 1,300 ringgit.

Prices for the whole of last year averaged 1,191.50 ringgit, down from the record high of 1,472.50 in 1995. Monthly average prices ranged from a high of 1,281 in May and a low of 1,066.50 in July. Prices started off at 1,245 in January and ended at 1,223 in December. PK prices, in contrast, rose to 806.50 ringgit last year from 737 ringgit in 1995. This was attributed entirely to strenth in CNO prices generated by a sharp drop in production and exports of CNO from the Philippines.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
